history.summary: A jumbo 2,906 sqft unit in Sengkang (D19) asking $1,032 psf vs a verified ~$1,495 psf project average — a large nominal discount, but it is a size artefact: jumbo units structurally trade far lower psf, the algo has ZERO same-size comparables, and the ~$3M quantum on a 99-yr (2005) lease has narrow exit liquidity.
history.rating_rationale: Web-verified recent Quartz transactions average ~$1,495 psf (range $1,417-$1,584), so the $1,032 psf headline looks like a ~31% bargain and drives the algo's -35.7% age-adj signal and the 'very_low_psf' flag. But psf_cohort_txns=0 — there is no same-size band to compare against, so the -32.2% vs-cohort number is a data quirk, exactly the trap to be skeptical of. This is a 2,906 sqft jumbo (a comparable jumbo is asking $3.3M), and giant units always carry a deep psf discount versus the regular-sized units that set the $1,495 average — so the discount is largely mechanical, not free value. Lease is 99-yr from 2005 (~78 yrs left, built 2009). Catalyst is limited to existing Buangkok/Hougang MRT. For a 5-7yr investment, the ~$3M quantum + jumbo format means a small buyer pool and slow exit; the abundant space is a feature mainly for own-stay, not investment. Net: fairly priced for what it is, but not an investment bargain — Neutral.

history.summary: A 1,484 sqft 3BR at The Quartz (D19 Sengkang, 99yr from Apr-2005, 240-270m to Buangkok NE15) asking $1.89M / $1,274 psf — headline -14% vs the project's URA median and -17% vs its own current core-stock price index of ~$1,550 psf. The project's own prints show that gap is MAJORITY ARTIFACT, not value: at The Quartz size carries no psf discount inside the core 1,022-1,380 sqft stock (larger is if anything +1%), but the 11 prints at 1,380+ sqft trade ~11-14% under the index when they sit on floors 01-05 and roughly at par when they sit high — and this listing's floor is unknown. The residual genuine discount is therefore ~8% (if low-floor/PES) to ~18% (if mid/high floor), not the 18% the 826 score is priced off. Compounding it: the listing has not been re-seen in 52 days while both sibling Quartz 3BRs were re-scraped on 2026-07-28, and the PropNex twin of the same 1,484 sqft unit at $1.85M now returns 'listing not found'.
history.rating_rationale: Not a Buy, and not an Avoid. The fundamentals are genuinely sound — OCR/D19 is the best-measured forward region (+3.7%/yr realized vs CCR +1.9%), the unit is real (bed_bands 'ok': 1,484 sqft sits inside The Quartz's own URA-filed 3BR band of 1,150-1,550 across 27 contracts; the project's floor-plan set runs 1,044-1,604 sqft), Buangkok NE15 at 240-270m is a real walkable-MRT signal, 625 units / 120 prints in 5yr is a deep book, and at 17 years old the unit sits squarely in the 7-30yr forward-return plateau so no age penalty is warranted. Three things stop it being a Buy. (1) THE DISCOUNT IS MOSTLY FORMAT, NOT VALUE. Decomposing all 120 Quartz prints against a half-yearly index built from core stock only: floor spread is 01-05 at -4.7% to 16-20 at +2.2%, size inside the core stock is flat-to-positive, but the 1,380+ sqft cohort on floors 01-05 prints at -8% to -19% (median ~-11%) — the classic PES/patio strata-area artifact. Against a like-for-like large low-floor comp escalated to today (~$1,380 psf → ~$2.05M) the ask is only ~8% cheap, not 18%. (2) THE ONE FACT THAT DECIDES THE CALL IS MISSING. floor_level is null (never detail-enriched, and PG serves it on only ~35-40% of listings) and facing is unobtainable; of the 11 large prints 6 were floors 01-05 and 5 were 11-20, so it is close to a coin flip whether the residual edge is 8% or 18%. (3) EXIT LIQUIDITY FOR THIS SIZE IS THIN. The 'very_deep' buyer-pool label describes the 1,050-1,250 sqft core; units 1,380+ sqft printed 11 times in 5 years (~2/yr, 9% of volume). A discount bought into a 2-sales-a-year cohort is the standard way an entry discount fails to convert into a return. Separately, the 826 / valuation 89 are overstated for this unit: the MMR is carried almost entirely by age_value 12.56 + psf_value 6.07 — the same cheap-vs-peers channel this decomposition shows is roughly 60% artifact. I am also explicitly NOT crediting the 6.38% trailing CAGR the record carries (current priors: trailing appreciation has ~0 forward power); I have overridden forward appreciation down to 4.2%. And the 2026-06-08 Buy on this same listing predates the v3.4.1 priors, credited that trailing CAGR as 'healthy', and did not test the large-unit/low-floor artifact — it should not be inherited. Finally, the practical answer to 'should you buy THIS unit at THIS price' is that the evidence says it is no longer on the market at this price. If it resurfaces, the entire call turns on one fact: at mid/high floor and <=$1.9M this upgrades to Buy; ground-floor PES at $1.89M is a fair-to-slightly-cheap price, not an edge.
red_flags: Listing appears off-market: seen once on 2026-06-07 and never again, while both sibling Quartz 3BRs were re-scraped 2026-07-28 and 301 D19 listings were seen since 2026-07-20 — so this is a delisting, not a scan-coverage gap. The PropNex twin of the same 1,484 sqft unit at $1.85M now returns 'listing not found'.

The -14%/-17% discount is majority artifact: 1,380+ sqft units on floors 01-05 at The Quartz print 8-19% under the project's core-stock index (PES/patio strata area), while size alone carries NO psf discount inside the core stock.
floor_level and facing are both null — the single fact that decides whether the residual discount is ~8% or ~18% is unknown, and PropertyGuru does not serve facing at all.
Thin exit cohort: only 11 prints at 1,380+ sqft in 5 years (~2/yr, 9% of the project's 120 prints). The 'very_deep' buyer-pool flag describes the 1,050-1,250 sqft core stock, not this unit.

score_1000 826 / valuation 89 are inflated for this unit — MMR is driven by age_value 12.56 + psf_value 6.07, the exact cheap-vs-peers channel shown here to be largely a format artifact. psf_cohort_txns is only 4.

Thin carry: 3.08% gross / 1.79% net, and the $4,850 rent is the project 3BR average (10 contracts) across ~1,150-1,350 sqft units — a 1,484 sqft unit does not rent proportionally more, so realised yield is likely ~3.2% at best.
99-yr lease from 18-Apr-2005: ~78 years left today, ~71 at a 5-7yr exit. Not near the CPF/financing cliff, but decaying and non-recoverable.
The prior 2026-06-08 Buy on this exact listing is stale and pre-v3.4.1 — it credited the 6.38% trailing CAGR as a forward edge and missed the large-unit/low-floor artifact. Do not inherit it.

Project momentum reads -0.753 (decelerating) — story only under current priors, but it does not support an above-baseline forward rate.
catalysts: OCR/D19 is the strongest measured forward region in the 28-district backtest (realized fwd OCR +3.7%/yr vs RCR +3.1%, CCR +1.9%) — this is a real, backtested tailwind, unlike the trailing CAGR.
Genuinely cheap vs district peers even after the artifact haircut: -16.9% vs the age-adjusted D19 median (size band 1400-1800). Cheap-vs-peers is the single most robust forward signal in the panel.

The large-unit discount at The Quartz has been closing: 1,380+ sqft prints ran -29% (2021) → -19/-14/-8% (2023) → -8/+1% (2024) → +8% (Dec-2025, 1,442 sqft at $1,656 psf / $2.389M, the highest psf in the whole 24-month set). Mean reversion in this cohort is the specific thesis for this unit — but it rests on ~11 prints.
Buangkok NE15 at 240-270m — a genuine walkable-MRT effect (as-of-T std_beta -0.11), anchoring resale demand.
Project price index is up strongly: core-stock median psf $1,340 (2024 H1) → $1,550 (2026 H1), +16% in two years.
Sengkang BTOs from 2018-2020 reaching MOP through 2023-2025 feed a steady stream of HDB upgraders into exactly this stock — 3BR family-sized private units at a sub-$2M quantum.

$1.85-1.89M for 1,484 sqft is a lot of space per dollar in 2026: the same quantum buys ~1,195 sqft of core Quartz stock at market psf (+24% space for the same money) — a real own-stay/upgrader draw if the floor is decent.
Cross Island Line Defu station ~1.05km and the wider Punggol Digital District — narrative only; the future-infrastructure score has no measured forward power, so this is not credited as edge.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Adequate but thin, and weaker than the headline. The $4,850/mo estimate is well-evidenced for the project (ura_project_bed, 10 contracts, 12mo, confidence 0.95) but it is the 3BR average across ~1,150-1,350 sqft units; rent does not scale linearly with strata area, so a 1,484 sqft unit realistically fetches ~$5,000-5,200 — roughly 3.2% gross, ~1.8% net. Tenant demand around Buangkok is steady HDB-adjacent family and mid-income professional stock rather than an expat pocket, so occupancy should be reliable and rent growth unremarkable. Note the prior direction of travel: high gross yield predicts LOWER forward price growth (std_beta -0.16), so a 3.1% yield here is not itself a negative — it simply means this is a capital-growth position with carry that barely covers holding costs, not an income position.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: I am overriding the shipped 6.38% down to 4.2%. The 6.38% is a trailing 5yr URA CAGR measured entirely inside the 2021-26 bull regime, and current priors are explicit that trailing appreciation carries ~0 forward power (marginal +0.03 once clustered). My own resale-to-resale index of the project's core stock confirms the trailing number is real (median psf $1,143 in 2021 H2 → $1,550 in 2026 H1, ~7.0%/yr) but that is a regime readout, not a forecast. The defensible forward build is: OCR realized baseline +3.7%/yr, plus a modest increment for the one robust signal that survives clustering here — cheap-vs-district-peers at -16.9% age-adjusted — plus walkable MRT, minus lease decay from 78 years and minus the risk that the large-unit gap stops closing. That lands near 4.2%. The genuine upside case is unit-specific rather than market-wide: if the 1,380+ sqft cohort continues re-rating toward the core index the way the Dec-2025 print suggests, this unit captures an extra 8-15% one-off. That is a plausible thesis on 11 transactions, not an underwritable one, and the model as a whole explains <10% of forward variance.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No profile exists for The Quartz (stack_profile: not_researched) and the listing was never detail-enriched — floor_level and facing are both null. That is the central gap in this evaluation. What the project's own URA prints do establish: 1,484 sqft is a real Quartz layout (the floor-plan set runs 1,044-1,604 sqft; distinct transacted sizes include 1,410 / 1,420 / 1,442 / 1,453 / 1,506 / 1,517 / 1,539 / 1,550), and bed_bands returns 'ok' against the project's own URA-rental 3BR band of 1,150-1,550 sqft over 27 contracts — so this is not a relabelled or mis-scraped unit. The floor effect at The Quartz is modest overall (01-05 median -4.7% vs index, 16-20 +2.2%), but it interacts strongly with size: of the six 1,380+ sqft prints on floors 01-05, five printed -8% to -19% below index, whereas the four on floors 11-20 printed -8% to +8%. Any large low-floor unit here should be assumed to carry PES/patio strata area, which inflates sqft and deflates psf without adding equivalent value. Before acting on this unit the buyer must establish the floor and whether the area includes a PES — and run /research-development 'The Quartz' to build the stack profile properly.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: Own build, not a portal headline. Base = OCR realized forward baseline +3.7%/yr from the 28-district URA panel; increment for cheap-vs-age-adjusted-district-peers (-16.9%, the one robust clustered signal) and 240-270m MRT; haircut for 78yr lease decay and thin 1,380+ sqft exit cohort. Cross-checked against my own resale-to-resale index of The Quartz core stock (<1,380 sqft, half-yearly medians, $1,143 2021H2 → $1,550 2026H1 = ~7.0%/yr) — treated as bull-regime evidence that the market is healthy, NOT extrapolated forward. Explicitly rejects the shipped 6.38% ura_5yr_cagr as trailing-only.
